api-errors.description: What a failed control-plane request carries: its HTTP status, the whole error body parsed when it is a JSON object, the body's code, and its detail whole -- never the truncated line the message is -- so a structured refusal such as platform_image_required or plan_limit is readable without a new SDK release; and a message that never repeats what the body echoed

binary.description: Receiving binary frames: speech a hub rendered, and files: a compressed part of a WIRE-1 frame inflates to at most 32 MiB, and one that would inflate further, or is truncated, is refused

thalovant-embedded-c.reason: src/wire.c decodes JSON frames, not WIRE-1 bitstrings, so there is no bit reader to extend; the type-code table already knows bin=12. The real blocker is zlib: the encoder chooses per frame whether to compress the metadata, and taking a compression dependency into a -std=c99 -pedantic microcontroller target is a decision about this SDK's footprint rather than about parity. The clip itself is never compressed, so a decoder that refused compressed metadata would still deliver audio.

connection-admission.description: Waiting for a hub to admit a new connection by following the operation the create returned, no read running past the wait's deadline: ready is admitted, failed and timed_out are a failure with the operation's code, 404 and no operation at all are admitted at once, a 5xx is ridden out, a 429 is waited out for the retry_after_seconds it names (inside the problem's detail object, where the API puts it), else its Retry-After or RateLimit-Reset header, unless that is longer than the time left; a 401 or 403 is the API's own authentication error passed through, any other refusal of the wait a failure that keeps the status, code and detail, and an API out of reach the SDK's unreachable error; the deadline is a timeout that is both a connection error and a timeout and says the hub may still admit it later; and a link whose origin (scheme, host and port) is not the API's is never fetched.

thalovant-embedded-c.reason: Embedded C is a caller-buffer wire library without a control-plane HTTP client; the caller owns every request it would make.

connection-kinds.description: Creating a hub connection of a named kind (spec.connection_type, home_assistant among them) and deleting one: the kind must come back in the answer, and a client the API made without it is deleted before the call fails as unsupported; a 422 is unsupported only when its detail or code, or a validation error's loc or msg, names the field -- never its echoed input; 402 and 403 plan_limit are a plan refusal, 409 home_assistant_already_linked names the client that holds the link, and 401, 423 and 403 'Insufficient scopes' are an authentication refusal, each keeping the api-errors fields. Delete sends If-Match, reading the etag first when none is given, retries once on 412, and counts 404 as deleted.

conversation.description: Carrying a conversation between the turns of a named session, which a hub keeps nothing of

thalovant-embedded-c.reason: thalovant_ask_request takes a session_id string, not a session, and builds {"session":{"session_id":...}} itself -- there is nowhere to put converse_handlers and nothing to carry it into. Applicable the day the C API accepts an opaque session object; the carry itself is a pure function and would port directly.

device-login.description: Device sign-in one step at a time for a caller that runs its own loop: begin returns the code to show and the poll interval, sends a registered app's client_id when given (Home Assistant's is thalovant-home-assistant) and leaves it out otherwise, and leaves an empty scope list out of the request (the API requires at least one; none asks for its default); one poll is pending (with the interval, lengthened by five seconds for good on slow_down), expired, denied, or the approved token with its scopes, expiry and id, which the SDK keeps; any other failure carries the api-errors fields. The token a device login minted can revoke itself, and revoking it is idempotent: a 401 on its own revoke means it is already dead, and it is forgotten either way. Every sign-in sets the token id from its own answer, so a default revoke never reaches a token the SDK no longer holds. Verification URLs with credentials are refused, and neither the device code nor the token appears in an error. describe reads a pending sign-in by its user code as the approver sees it (GET /v1/auth/device/codes/{user_code}): scopes, client_name, client_id, device_name and client_verified, true only for a registered app. A token answer whose body is not a JSON object is an error with no status.

home-link.description: The Home Assistant link on the data plane: every thalovant.home.request is answered at most once with a thalovant.home.response, sent as an OVOS-MSG-1 §5.2 reply built from the context as the hub sent it (deep copy, destination the old source, source the old destination's first entry; no source means no destination); response_type and error_code come from the contract's lists, and a handler that raises, is too slow or answers outside them is failed_to_handle, timeout or unknown with empty speech. Everything happens within the hub's 10 s: the handler gets its timeout or what is left, the reply what the handler left, and a reply that would arrive late is never sent. speech is plain text made by one portable rule: real tags, comments and processing instructions removed (a '<' not opening one is text), then numeric references, the five XML entities and   decoded once and nothing else, then Unicode White_Space runs collapsed. Keeping the link up (link-keeping-vectors): a close with 1000, 1005 or 1008 during the handshake or within 750 ms after it, before the hub has sent anything that authenticates, is a refusal, its code allowed to surface up to 250 ms late; a Noise message that does not authenticate is a refusal, a failed KK attempt is followed at once by XX, and a hub key that is not the pinned one is a key-changed connection error, never a refusal; a hub that closes as an XX handshake ends has refused the client's own key (client_key_rejected, naming the key folders: re-pair, or share the key folder); the supervisor retries failures and refusals on a 10 s ladder doubling to 120 s, dials again at once after a drop, gives up on refusals that last 600 s, and stops at once on a changed hub key or a refused client key. A reply withdrawn while it waits behind another frame is never sent late and leaves the link as it was. Speech trims White_Space only.

identity.description: Secure client identity and credential handling within the host storage model. link-carriers.description: KK then XX on the carriers that are not a WebSocket: over HTTPS polling a failed KK attempt is an answer that does not authenticate or a request answered 401 or 403, and a 401 or 403 while or right after an XX handshake completes is the hub refusing the client's own key; over MQTT only an answer that does not authenticate, since a broker relays no refusal. The XX attempt follows at once in the same connect, and its outcome is the connect's.
